text: Digital circuits resist the accumulation of noise because each stage regenerates a clean, full-strength signal instead of passing degradation along.
explanation: This is why a processor can run billions of operations per second for years and stay exact. Because only two states are legitimate, a gate handed a degraded 2.9 V does not emit a degraded output — it emits a fresh full-strength high generated locally, discarding the error. Analogue systems cannot do this, which is why a photocopy of a photocopy decays: nothing tells the machine which part was signal.
